source: JZ Mock C · Paper 2 · Question 12 · Publisher worked answer
label: JZ Mock C · Paper 2 · Question 12
knowledgePattern: Refute a functional conclusion while satisfying its hypothesis everywhere
solution:
For f(x)=sinx, odd symmetry gives (f(x)+f(−x))/2=0 for every real x, so the premise holds with a = 0.

However sine is not of the form kx: its value at π would force k = 0, while its value at π/2 is 1. Thus it violates the conclusion and is a counterexample.

The linear examples satisfy the conclusion. Tangent is not defined for every real input, and cosine has a nonconstant even part, so those fail the required premise/domain. Answer C.

hints.title: A counterexample needs two checks
hints.body: The function must satisfy the average condition for every real x, but fail to be a straight line of the stated form.
hints.recap: A counterexample meets the assumption and breaks the conclusion.
hints.pitfall: Being nonlinear is not enough: the given average condition must still hold.
hints.pause: For each candidate, first calculate its value at the negative input.

recall.reminder: A counterexample meets the assumption and breaks the conclusion.

hints.title: Check the average and the domain
hints.body: Work out [f(x)+f(−x)]/2 for each candidate. Does the result stay constant as x changes? Is the function defined at every real input?
hints.recap: Sine and cosine have different symmetries, and tangent has excluded inputs.
hints.pitfall: Check the all-real domain before accepting a candidate.
hints.pause: Among the functions that pass those checks, show which one cannot be the proposed straight line.

recall.reminder: Use the sine/cosine symmetries and remember that tangent is not defined at every real input.
